title: Effect of Bilingual Instructional Method in the Academic Achievement of Junior Secondary School Students in Mathematics
extended_summary:
This study examines whether using a bilingual instructional method improves junior secondary school students’ achievement in mathematics compared with conventional monolingual instruction. The paper is motivated by persistent low mathematics performance and argues that language of instruction may be a barrier to understanding mathematical concepts, especially for students in multilingual settings.

The intervention was a bilingual teaching module: a mathematics teaching module originally developed in English and then translated into Igbo by a mathematics expert with Igbo proficiency. The study used a non-equivalent control group quasi-experimental design with intact classes. The target population was JSS1 students in Abia State, Nigeria, and the sample came from two public secondary schools in Ohafia Local Government Area. Students in the experimental group received bilingual instruction, while the control group received conventional instruction; both groups took a pre-test and post-test using a researcher-developed Mathematics Achievement Test.

Findings indicated that students taught with the bilingual instructional method scored higher than those taught with the conventional method on the post-test. The analysis also found no significant main effect of gender, though there was a significant interaction effect between instructional method and gender. The authors conclude that bilingual instruction is an effective and gender-fair approach for improving mathematics achievement in this context and recommend broader adoption by schools and policymakers.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a quasi-experimental non-equivalent control group study, not a randomized trial. It has a defined intervention and outcome measure, but there are notable internal validity concerns from non-randomization and attrition, so it fits yellow rather than green or blue.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported gain in mathematics achievement is positive but modest and based on a small single-study sample from one local context. No standardized effect size is reported, and the result is not directly about AI or ChatGPT, so broader impact is unclear.

finding.finding_summary: A quasi-experimental study of junior secondary school students in Nigeria (n=38 completing the study; initially 76) found that bilingual instructional method improved mathematics achievement compared with conventional instruction. Post-test MAT performance was higher for the bilingual group, with a mean difference of 4.83 in favor of bilingual instruction and a statistically significant ANCOVA result (F=50.357, p=0.000).
finding.measure: Mathematics Achievement Test (MAT) post-test scores; ANCOVA-adjusted comparison of bilingual vs conventional instruction
finding.study_size: n=38 completing the study (20 experimental, 18 control)
